title: Raqiya: The New Book of Revelation
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: After a crash in the Nevada desert kills her family, the sole survivor Luna Hazuki makes a pact with a mysterious being in a morgue, and seven years later her family is alive again (AniList/MangaDex blurb; Otaku USA review). The pact is set to lead to an apocalypse; MangaUpdates says God descends to Earth in the form of a girl. Otaku USA notes the story draws heavily on Gnosticism.
life_message: It asks whether love for one's family can justify a bargain with forces beyond human control, and treats that question as world-shaking.

folkways.japan: A Japanese creative team set much of the story in America and draws on Christian and Gnostic imagery, which in Japanese manga often serves as exotic myth rather than confession.

delivery.evidence: Otaku USA: volume 1 is mystery with little explanation; religious ideas carried by plot (to verify).
delivery.note: Religious ideas appear mostly as plot mechanics in the first volume; later treatment is unknown.

winners_losers: Luna gains her family back at a cosmic cost; whether any worldview is vindicated by the apocalypse is not stated in the sources.
to_verify: Otaku USA reviews volume 1 only; later volumes' handling of God and Christianity unverified.
